pr_title: prevent firefox marking required textareas invalid
pr_body:
Bug was caused by an IE10/IE11 bugfix dealing with the placeholder attribute and textContent. Solved by avoiding the IE bugfix when textContent was empty.

Closes #16402 

## Test Plan

Open up DOM test fixtures and compare (in Firefox)...

local: http://screeching-degree.surge.sh/textareas
to latest: http://screeching-degree.surge.sh/textareas?version=16.9.0

...and verify that textareas are no longer marked invalid on load when required.

Also confirm that the original IE bugfix is still functioning as intended.
pr_comments: @aweary no worries if you can't get to it, just flagging you about the original IE10/11 fix back in https://github.com/facebook/react/commit/4dd625a93f2d06f801a896d364da15719498cb95.

No significant bundle size changes to report.

issue_context.title: textarea with `required` attribute renders in invalid state in FF
issue_context.body:
*Bug*

When a `textarea` has the `required` attribute it renders in the invalid state using FireFox. 

This behavior is visible here: https://codesandbox.io/s/rough-frog-f00ow. Remember to view it in FireFox.  

I expect the required field to validate on form submit and not before. 

I have tested this with FireFox 68 and 69 and React 16.8.6

This appears appears to be a re-occurrence of: https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/8395
comments:
Uh oh. There was a fix for this for inputs, but the textarea code path is different:

https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/0da7bd0604a5be7f96572b9f75d16fef5674bc5d/packages/react-dom/src/client/ReactDOMInput.js#L269-L277

This probably needs to happen on the textarea side too. Probably somewhere in here:
https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/0da7bd0604a5be7f96572b9f75d16fef5674bc5d/packages/react-dom/src/client/ReactDOMTextarea.js#L149-L162

I think I can fix this pretty quickly, but won't be able to get to it until later in the week if anyone else would like to pick it up.
Just talked with @halvves about taking a stab at this!

review_comments:
For others - we pulled this test from `ReactDOMInput-test.js`, which uses a similar technique to check mutations for an iOS Safari date bug.

I still think this is a weird test, and I wonder if it makes sense to create a common helper for this sort of thing.
